findings.claim: Generated code for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets is not decorated. Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and in netstandard2.0, and it can target classes there. So the exclusion is unnecessary and breaks the criterion 'All generated code is decorated' for a large share of consumers (netstandard2.0 libraries, .NET Framework apps). The README documents the gap rather than closing it.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDownlevelTargetTests.GeneratedTypesAreExcludedWhenTargetSymbolIsDefined (NETSTANDARD2_0 / NETFRAMEWORK). The generated formatter and resolver types lack the attribute, so the test fails on head. Supporting premise: resolve ReferenceAssemblies.NetStandard.NetStandard20 and ReferenceAssemblies.NetFramework.Net472.Default and show that compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName("System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute") is non-null.

findings.claim: The new opt-out does not apply to composite resolvers. CompositeResolverTemplate emits `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on the composite resolver and its FormatterCache<T> unconditionally, while every other template checks Options.Generator.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The README says all generated resolvers carry the attribute and that `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage = false` opts out, but a composite resolver cannot be opted out.

receipt_plan.detail: CompositeResolverTemplate.tt lines 7-9 and 35-37 have no `<# if (Options.Generator.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage) #>` guard, unlike ResolverTemplate.tt, FormatterTemplate.tt, EnumTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt and StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt. README.md:1639-1641 promises a uniform opt-out.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate by default and add an opt-out. Every template emits the attribute unless the user opts out. The opt-out is a new public property `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` (default true), with PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt entries. It feeds `GeneratorOptions.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage` via AnalyzerUtilities, and each template guards its attribute emission with `if (Options.Generator.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage)`.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Decorate unconditionally with no setting, as the issue says a setting is not needed. Make it a minimal edit of A. Drop `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` from GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute and the four PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt files. Drop `GeneratorOptions.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage` and its AnalyzerUtilities mapping. Remove the `<# if (...) #>` guards so every template, like CompositeResolverTemplate already does, always writes `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. Remove the opt-out sentence from the README. This adds no public API surface.
